### DocTestSyntaxError

Thrown when a doc test or feature file breaks the conventions the generator relies on. The
message starts with `file:line:column`, so editors and CI logs link straight to it.

##### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

###### Inherited from

```ts
Error.stackTraceLimit;
```

#### Methods

##### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack; // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

###### Parameters

###### targetObject

`object`

###### constructorOpt?

`Function`

###### Returns

`void`

###### Inherited from


### DocPage

A tutorial or how-to page parsed from one doc test file. The page structure mirrors
the test structure, so a test that passes is proof that every sample on the page works.

#### Properties

##### intro

```ts
readonly intro: string;
```

Markdown from the file-level JSDoc block. Empty when there is none.

##### sections

```ts
readonly sections: readonly DocSection[];
```

One per `it()` or `test()` inside the `describe()`, in source order.

##### setup

```ts
readonly setup: readonly CodeSample[];
```

Regions outside the `describe()`, rendered after the intro. They hold definitions that
several sections share, such as a configured instance or a helper class.

##### title

```ts

```

The name of the file's single top-level `describe()`.

## Functions

### checkDocs()

```ts
function checkDocs(packageDir): DocsReport;
```

Runs every documentation check on one package: export coverage, link integrity,
Diátaxis compliance, and requirement traceability through the feature files. Each problem names the file or export it is about, so the report
is a to-do list rather than a score.

#### Parameters

##### packageDir

`string`

#### Returns

[`DocsReport`](#docsreport)

---

### generateDocs()

```ts
function generateDocs(packageDir): Promise<string[]>;
```

Writes the generated documentation of one package into `docs/`:

- `docs/tutorials/` and `docs/how-to/` from the doc tests in `tests/docs/`. Both
  directories are wiped first, so a deleted doc test deletes its page.
- The generated header on every TypeDoc page in `docs/reference/`. Run TypeDoc first.
- `docs/reference/specifications/` from the Gherkin files in `features/`, wiped first
  like the doc test quadrants.
- `docs/README.md`, the index of all four quadrants. `docs/explanation/` is hand-written
  and only read, for page titles.

Every written file goes through Prettier, so the output passes the repo format check
without a separate formatting step.

#### Parameters

##### packageDir

`string`

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`[]\>

The written paths, relative to `packageDir`.

---

### parseDocTest()

```ts
function parseDocTest(sourceText, sourcePath): DocPage;
```

Parses one doc test file into a page. The file must hold exactly one top-level
`describe()` (the page title) whose direct children are plain `it()` or `test()`
calls (the sections). Any other shape throws, so a malformed doc test fails
`just generate` instead of silently producing a broken page.

#### Parameters

##### sourceText

`string`

##### sourcePath

`string`

#### Returns

[`DocPage`](#docpage)

#### Throws

when the file breaks a convention.
